T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural supply chain chokepoints, persistent rare earth pricing near record highs, systemic compliance friction

Synopsis:
Some Chinese rare earth suppliers are voluntarily halting shipments to US buyers, spooked by Beijing's August 2025 sanctions on the RBA and broader geopolitical entanglement risk. This compounds existing export licence delays on strategically sensitive materials (yttrium, indium phosphide, tungsten, terbium, gallium), with some US firms waiting 6+ months for approvals. Japan is being hit hardest — effectively cut off from several key minerals. The issue is on the US-China summit agenda for Xi's September 24 Washington visit, with market participants anticipating a tactical easing of controls around the summit to reduce diplomatic pressure, though structural supply chain fragility persists.
